open_points.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.subject: service-operation rights table
open_points.text: `release_declarations` owns “A09 rule 2's table of the services, their operations and their highest classes”; `service_access` owns “the service's operations and highest class from the release (A09 rules 1, 2, 3)”; the changed `operations` passage calls it “the release's table alone”.
open_points.question: Who owns the service-to-operations and highest-class facts: `release_declarations`, or `service_access`? If `service_access` owns only authentication and the decision returned by `service_may_call`, the text must distinguish that mechanism from ownership of the table.
options: `release_declarations` owns the table; `service_access` only queries and enforces it
`service_access` owns the table; `release_declarations` only supplies release material
Both keep representations, with a stated synchronization rule
open_points.default_guess: Treat `release_declarations` as the sole owner of the table and `service_access` as its enforcing consumer.

open_points.subject: owner's right to invoke an operation
open_points.text: “The operation table: every operation of either surface with its stages and the modules it changes — not which service may call it ...; the owner's operations are the owner interface's.” Stage (1) nevertheless includes “the caller's authentication and its right to the operation”, while `owner_interface` says “Must not own: Any check the server makes: the forms carry values, `operations` decides.”
open_points.question: Which module owns the authoritative set of operations the owner may invoke, and which module enforces it at stage (1)? The changed text explains service authorization through `service_access` but leaves owner-operation authorization between `operations` and `owner_interface`, whose stated responsibilities point in opposite directions.
options: `operations` owns and enforces an owner-operation allowlist
`owner_interface` owns and enforces the allowed route set before calling `operations`
Another earlier module owns the owner-operation declarations and `operations` enforces them
open_points.default_guess: Allow only explicit owner-interface routes corresponding to State 0 actions whose `who` includes the owner, and never expose a generic owner dispatcher.

witness.initial: The owner has a valid owner session; no agent session with identity S is registered.
events: The owner sends a crafted owner-interface request asking to perform `register an agent session` for S, an operation State 0 assigns to Cabinet Kernel.
`owner_interface` and `operations` process the request according to their respective readings of who owns the owner's operation set.
outcomes: An implementation treating the owner interface's explicit routes as the authoritative set refuses the request before dispatch because registration is not an owner operation.
An implementation treating `operations`' operation table as dispatchable after a valid owner-session check accepts it, because no owner-operation allowlist is specified there, and registers S.
witness.observer: The owner sees S in the session list; Cabinet Kernel also sees whether S is already registered.
